title: Tenant Autosurgeon: heuristic prefill presets and conservative quantization filter
author: Jordan Patel
release_notes: Introduce tenant-level auto-suggestions for prefill/batching defaults and a conservative quantization 'sieve' that proposes tenant-specific quant profiles with safe rollback. Admin CLI and dry-run mode included. Backfill for existing tenants is optional and gated by rollout flag.
description: Motivation: smaller tenants and bursty workloads were frequently assigned overly aggressive quantization profiles and batch defaults which produced intermittent regressions in generation quality and sometimes spiked latency during cold starts. This PR adds a tenant-aware 'Autosurgeon' service that synthesizes prefill/batch/caching presets and a conservative quantization filter ("quant-sieve") to propose safer, tenant-scoped defaults. The work includes: 1) a long-running service (services/autosurgeon) to synthesize profiles from recent replayed traffic and signal heuristics, 2) an HTTP/CLI dry-run API to preview suggested presets and run local cost/loss simulations, 3) integration with tenant-defaults store + safe rollout flags, 4) telemetry hooks and a compact eval harness for held-out prompt sets, and 5) a UI hook to preview and accept suggestions in Console. Checklist: [x] Design doc added (pkg/autosurgeon/DESIGN.md) [x] Unit tests for core heuristics [x] Integration test for tenant-defaults write path [x] Dry-run CLI and RBAC gating [x] Telemetry metrics + traces [x] Rollout plan and rollback path. Implementation notes: Autosurgeon is intentionally conservative by default: quant-sieve produces multiple ranked profiles (fp16 -> int8-ish -> int4-light) with estimated unit-econ deltas and quality deltas; the platform applies only tenant-accepted suggestions or automatic suggestions when tenant usage patterns fall into low-risk bins. Testing: local unit/integration tests, synthetic replay runs against the prefiller simulator, and a staged canary on two low-traffic tenants. Performance: runtime overhead of autosurgeon service is negligible since analysis is asynchronous; the path that writes tenant defaults is guarded by safety gates and feature flags. See commits summary and changed-files for details. Merge: squashed and merged after CI turned green and reviewers signed off.

conversation: Maya Singh: Nice end-to-end, can you explicitly call out how retention of replay data affects suggestions? We should not hold more than 30 days by default.
Jordan Patel: Good call — default retention is 14 days. I added a config knob and doc note in ops/autosurgeon-rollout.md.
Ethan Cole: Please add a test that asserts the sieve never suggests aggressive int4 for tenants with <1000 tokens/day. Also add an e2e that exercises dry-run path.
Jordan Patel: Added token-threshold test and a dry-run integration test that runs the synthesizer against a 2-hour replay segment in CI.
Priya Rao: Verified metrics and smoke-tested on the canary tenants; approving pending CI flakiness fix.

Priya Rao: Merged via squash after CI green.
rollout_plan: Week 0: deploy autosurgeon to infra and enable dry-run for all orgs. Week 1: enable autosurgeon suggestions for opt-in tenants (low traffic) and collect quality telemetry. Week 2: enable auto-suggestions for low-risk tenants with automatic mild quant profiles. Week 4: gradual expansion gated by eval pass rate and SLO monitors.
rollback_procedure: Disable autosurgeon writer feature-flag and revert tenant-defaults by applying last-known-good snapshot from tenant-defaults-backups. Alerts and automatic rollback via the console if quality regressions exceed 0.5% on held-out eval sets.
testing_notes: Added a small offline eval harness (pkg/autosurgeon/eval_harness.go) that runs suggested profiles against tenant-specific held-out prompts. CI runs the harness in integration stage with a synthetic dataset. Load tests show no difference in serving latency when autosurgeon is active.
